_comment: Player-facing tunables. Nothing here was recovered from the 1990 binary. Every value is a stand-in the owner accepted or set, and every one is meant to be changed by editing this file, not by editing code.

notes.roundSeconds: 5 s chosen 2026-11-06 by the owner. At 1 cell per round the Washington-Moscow march is ~104 cells, about 8.7 minutes. The original felt like a campaign, not a 24-second war, and 0.14 s made income land every 3.5 s.
notes.payEvery: Rounds between income payments. 25 rounds at 5 s is just over two minutes.
notes.prices: Only two relations were recovered: a tank is twice an infantry, a nuke is 10. The rest are stand-ins.
notes.fuel: STAND-IN. The archive's fuel reserve and burn were never recovered: 10000 reserve and 1 per round are invented and are here only so a side can run short. Per side, deliberately not the desktop archive's single shared reserve. Fuel is now one entry in `resources`, not a block of its own.
notes.steel: STAND-IN, an owner-designed expansion and not a recovery: the 1990 game had oil only. 40 held and 1 a round are invented so a second kind can be held and consumed. No yield is set on purpose: the archive never recovered one, so the server refuses to hand out steel rather than guess a number. Gated to 1942 and 1986; the other scenarios do not carry it.
notes.hits: The archive's HITS is 6. Do not raise it: the desktop Washington-to-Moscow march meets one cell short and Red holds both capitals.
notes.air: The 8 and 4 are the booklet counts (docs/POLISH_LOOP.md: air mission inactive 8 rounds, scramble 4). The reach of 10 is a STAND-IN: the archive's aircraft range was not recovered.
notes.nukes: A nuke is refused by default and the archive's own stand-in deals no damage and paints no wasteland. exclusion 2 is a STAND-IN guard around a capital; the archive kept a home-ground guard but never printed its size. The launch limit (three fired or three absorbed) is the booklet count and stays in code.
notes.overrun: Overrun existed in the archive (the owner's list of missing combat depth names it); how much more force it took was never recovered. The rule therefore compares counts rather than inventing a threshold: when one side has strictly more friendly pieces standing on the defender's cell than the defender has, the defender is removed at once. Set false to return to a pure grinding front.
